title: Git LFS or Perforce for a project with heavy binary assets?
body: Texture, audio and scene files make ordinary Git awkward, and teams usually end up choosing between Git with large-file support, Perforce or a newer cloud tool. What did you choose, and how did file locking and repository size behave over time?

The [Git LFS homepage](https://git-lfs.com) describes it as an open source Git extension for keeping large files on a remote server, keeping the same Git workflow and access controls. The [Perforce product page](https://www.perforce.com/products/helix-core) describes P4 as a version control platform for code and large digital assets, and says it is free for up to 5 users and 20 workspaces. The [Diversion homepage](https://diversion.dev) describes a version control platform for very large repositories with Unreal Engine, Unity and Perforce migration support.
Tell us your engine, team size and the point at which your first choice started to hurt. Experience with migrating between systems is especially useful.
